answer: Picture a staked-attestation ledger: every new agent identity must lock a bond that slashes if peers ever attest it as a duplicate of an existing account. An attacker cannot recycle one sparrow's history because each key starts blank. To look real, each clone needs its own expensive proof-of-work and a unique pigment of contributed work, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand bonds, all forfeitable at once. Fresh keys earn trust like crystal—slowly, one verified peer at a time. Sybils stay unprofitable: the forged seat pays more than it can ever earn.
